parts.title: Historian Hysteria
parts.summary: Reconcile two equal-length columns of integer location IDs by sorting each list independently in ascending order, pairing elements by rank, and summing the absolute differences across all pairs.
parts.algorithmSummary: Typed-array numeric sort & linear zip: copy left and right columns from immutable LocationLists into private Float64Arrays, call native numeric .sort(), and sum |L[i] - R[i]| with safe-integer overflow validation; differentially verified against a 1D Wasserstein CDF sweep oracle.
parts.complexity: O(N log N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Preserving raw unsorted left and right columns in 2024/day01/shared/LocationLists keeps Part 2 frequency similarity zero-churn.
Sorting private Float64Array copies avoids JavaScript's lexicographic Array.prototype.sort() footgun while covering all safe integers.
A 1D Wasserstein CDF sweep over net multiplicities provides a completely independent differential test oracle for rank-paired distances.

parts.title: Historian Hysteria
parts.summary: Compute the similarity score between the two location ID columns by multiplying each left-column ID by its frequency in the right column and summing across all left-column entries.
parts.algorithmSummary: Right-column hash frequency map with exact BigInt accumulation: count right-column multiplicities in one O(N) pass, then scan raw left entries accumulating BigInt(id) * BigInt(rightCount) with zero churn to 2024/day01/shared; differentially verified against a sorted two-pointer merge oracle.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Converting operands to BigInt before multiplying (BigInt(id) * BigInt(count)) prevents silent IEEE-754 overflow on arbitrary safe-integer inputs.
Scaling BigInt coordinates in BigInt ((val - min) * 1_000_000n / span) before Number conversion keeps SVG score curves exact across huge ranges.

parts.title: Red-Nosed Reports
parts.summary: Count how many reactor level reports are strictly monotonic (all ascending or all descending) with every adjacent difference between 1 and 3 inclusive.
parts.algorithmSummary: Single-pass directional scan on immutable Report entities in 2024/day02/shared/: derive trend on pair 0 and short-circuit on the first StepFailure (flat, reversal, or jump), differentially verified against a delta-range envelope oracle across 1,000 synthetic reports.
parts.complexity: O(N * L) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Separating TrendDirection (1 | -1) from flat pair 0 (trend === null) and scanning from index 0 cleanly catches flat starts and initial jumps while leaving isSafeStep reusable for Part 2 bridged checks.
Computing delta, length, trend, and isSafe dynamically on frozen StepFailure and Report value objects eliminates derived-state drift.

parts.title: Red-Nosed Reports
parts.summary: Apply the Problem Dampener allowing at most one level to be omitted from each report, and count how many reports are natively safe or become strictly safe after deleting a single level.
parts.algorithmSummary: Localized first-failure candidate probe reusing 2024/day02/shared with zero churn: if Report.firstFailure() occurs at index k, test minimal ascending skip candidates ([0, 1, 2] when k === 1 to catch index-0 trend flips, else [k, k + 1]) in O(N * L) time and O(1) auxiliary space; differentially verified against an exhaustive O(N * L^2) brute-force oracle across 1,000 reports.
parts.complexity: O(N * L) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: When Report.firstFailure() triggers at index k === 1, removing index 0 can reverse the inferred initial trend and rescue the report; probing [0, 1, 2] for k === 1 and [k, k + 1] otherwise is provably exact and minimal.
Modeling DampenerOutcome as a discriminated union makes inconsistent states (such as unsafe with a removedIndex) compile-time impossible.

parts.title: Mull It Over
parts.summary: Scan a continuous corrupted program memory stream for exact mul(X,Y) calls with 1-to-3-digit unsigned integer operands, ignore all malformed fragments, and sum all valid products.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-backtracking single-pass charCodeAt lexer in 2024/day03/shared/ tokenizing mul(X,Y), do(), and don't() into a frozen ParsedMemory stream in O(N) time; differentially verified against a global RegExp matchAll oracle over adversarial nested prefixes and a 20 KB synthetic corpus.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(K) token space
learnings: Returning the exact mismatch cursor c (not c + 1) in a charCodeAt lexer preserves inner starts of nested prefixes like mul(mul(2,3)) and don'tdon't() with zero backtracking.
Scanning raw memory continuously without line splitting and tokenizing do()/don't() up front keeps Part 2 conditional execution zero-churn.

parts.title: Mull It Over
parts.summary: Execute the same continuous corrupted memory stream while honoring do() and don't() conditional gates (starting enabled and persisting across newlines), summing X * Y only for enabled mul(X,Y) instructions.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn stateful token fold over 2024/day03/shared ParsedMemory.instructions in O(K) time and O(1) auxiliary space, exposing computeInstructionStates so the visualizer never re-implements the gate state machine; differentially verified against a raw-text streaming-skip oracle over a 20 KB synthetic corpus.
parts.complexity: O(N) parse, O(K) fold, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Tokenizing do() and don't() alongside mul(X,Y) in 2024/day03/shared made Part 2 a pure O(K) fold with zero parser edits and exact cross-line gate persistence.
Exporting computeInstructionStates from domain keeps the React tape and gate-ribbon visualizer thin without duplicating conditional state logic.

parts.title: Ceres Search
parts.summary: Search a rectangular 2D grid of uppercase letters for all straight-line occurrences of the word XMAS in all 8 compass directions (horizontal, vertical, and diagonal, forward and backward), allowing overlapping letters and shared endpoints.
parts.algorithmSummary: X-origin 8-direction ray scan reusing shared/core Grid2D and DIRS_8 via an immutable WordSearchGrid wrapper in 2024/day04/shared/ with O(1) convex-box endpoint bounds checks; differentially verified against an independent 4-axis scanline bidirectional window oracle over seeded rectangular grids up to 40x30.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Wrapping Grid2D<string> in WordSearchGrid with a generic matchesAt(row, col, dr, dc, word) and convex-box endpoint bounds check handles all 8 directions in Part 1 and leaves Part 2 diagonal X-MAS checks zero-churn.
Validating non-negative endpoints inside WordMatch makes invalid negative-coordinate rays unrepresentable while keeping endRow, endCol, and cells dynamically derived.

parts.title: Ceres Search
parts.summary: Count every 3x3 X-MAS cross centered on 'A' whose two diagonal arms (NW-SE and NE-SW) each spell MAS either forwards or backwards, ignoring orthogonal neighbors and allowing overlapping corners.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn interior 'A'-center diagonal-pair classifier reusing 2024/day04/shared WordSearchGrid in O(R * C) time: validates each diagonal independently against {M, S} into four XMasOrientation variants with zero char-code collision risk; differentially verified against a top-left 3x3 WordSearchGrid.matchesAt oracle up to 40x30.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(K) space
learnings: Checking each diagonal independently against exact 'M'/'S' pairs avoids both the MAM/SAS corner-count trap (M.S/.A./S.M) and ASCII sum collisions like 'P'+'P' === 'M'+'S'.
Driving XMasCross.diagonals from a total Record<XMasOrientation, ...> lookup table keeps every orientation branch covered with zero unreachable switch defaults.

parts.title: Print Queue
parts.summary: Given page ordering rules X|Y and odd-length print updates, identify every update that satisfies all applicable ordering rules (where both X and Y appear in the update) and return the sum of their middle page numbers.
parts.algorithmSummary: Per-update O(L^2) pairwise reverse-rule check on an immutable PageOrderRules adjacency index in 2024/day05/shared/ (avoiding global topological sort because the 49-page rule graph is a regular cyclic tournament) while exposing inducedGraph via shared/core DirectedGraph for zero-churn Part 2 repair; differentially verified against a raw rule-scan position-map oracle across cyclic tournaments and 30 random inputs.
parts.complexity: O(R + sum L_u^2) time, O(R + L_max) space
learnings: The personal input's global rule graph on 49 pages has 1,176 = C(49, 2) edges with every vertex at in-degree 24 and out-degree 24 (a regular cyclic tournament), so all ordering checks and topological sorts must be scoped to each update's induced subgraph.

Checking all pairs (i < j) instead of only adjacent pairs catches non-adjacent violations on sparse partial orders while exposing PageOrderRules.inducedGraph for zero-churn Part 2 repair via shared/core DirectedGraph.

parts.title: Print Queue
parts.summary: Filter to only the invalid print updates, reorder each update to satisfy all applicable page ordering rules, and return the sum of the middle page numbers of the repaired updates.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn per-update induced DAG topological repair reusing 2024/day05/shared PageOrderRules.inducedGraph and shared/core DirectedGraph.topologicalOrder in O(R + U * L^2) time: handles both transitive tournaments and sparse partial orders while detecting induced cycles cleanly; differentially verified against both a pairwise-comparator sort oracle and a tournament in-degree ranking oracle across 30 seeded tournaments.
parts.complexity: O(R + U * L^2) time, O(R + L^2) space
learnings: Reusing PageOrderRules.inducedGraph(update.pages).topologicalOrder() via shared/core DirectedGraph gave Part 2 zero-churn repair that stays sound on sparse DAGs and throws loudly on induced cycles.
Omitting redundant empty-list early returns when sampleTraceIndices(0, maxSteps) natively produces [] keeps tracePrintRepairs branch-minimal with 100% v8 coverage.

parts.title: Guard Gallivant
parts.summary: Simulate a patrolling guard on a 2D floorplan who turns 90 degrees clockwise in place whenever blocked by an obstacle and otherwise steps forward, counting distinct cells visited before leaving the map.
parts.algorithmSummary: Flat Uint8Array 4-bit direction-mask patrol engine in 2024/day06/shared/ built on shared/core Grid2D and clockwise DIRS_4 in O(R * C) time: handles multi-turn corners in place without forced steps, detects loops via bitmask collisions, and supports optional extraObstacle for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against an independent Set-based reference simulator across 20 seeded random grids.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Re-evaluating the facing direction in place on every turn (instead of stepping after a single 90-degree rotation) cleanly handles 2-, 3-, and 4-wall corners and catches boxed-in loops.
Packing 4-bit direction masks in a flat Uint8Array(R * C) gives O(1) loop detection and exposes LabMap + simulatePatrol(map, { extraObstacle }) for zero-churn Part 2 reuse.

parts.title: Guard Gallivant
parts.summary: Count how many single-cell obstruction placements (excluding the guard's starting position and existing obstacles) force the patrolling guard into an infinite loop.
parts.algorithmSummary: Jump-table directional raycasting reusing 2024/day06/shared LabMap and simulatePatrol with zero churn: restricts candidates to the baseline patrol's visited cells, precomputes 4 flat Int32Array stop tables with O(1) extra-obstacle ray interception, and detects cycles via a method-local generation-stamped Uint32Array(4 * R * C) in O(R * C + K * T) time (11.17 ms across 4,655 candidates); differentially verified against simulatePatrol across fixed edge grids and 20 seeded random floorplans.
parts.complexity: O(R * C + K * T) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Restricting obstruction candidates to the baseline patrol's visited cells (excluding start) plus 4-directional Int32Array jump tables cuts 130x130 loop search from hundreds of milliseconds down to 11.17 ms on the main thread.
Using a method-local generation-stamped Uint32Array(4 * R * C) keeps ObstacleJumpTable 100% immutable and re-entrant while avoiding per-candidate zero-fill overhead.

parts.title: Bridge Repair
parts.summary: Determine which calibration equations can produce their target integer by inserting '+' or '*' between adjacent operands evaluated strictly left-to-right (no operator precedence), and return the sum of targets for all solvable equations.
parts.algorithmSummary: Right-to-left inverse pruned DFS parameterized by a polymorphic CalibrationOperator interface in 2024/day07/shared/ using exact BigInt arithmetic end-to-end (3.52 ms across 850 equations), paired with a pure-TS treeLayout engine and reusable BridgeRepairVisualizer in 2024/day07/shared/viz/ for zero-churn Part 2 concatenation reuse; differentially verified against an independent left-to-right forwardPrunedSolve oracle across 100 seeded equations, operand-1 traps, and >2^60 targets.
parts.complexity: O(M * 2^(k-1)) worst-case, ~O(M * k) typical time, O(k) space
learnings: Right-to-left inverse branching (checking divisibility for '*' before subtracting for '+') prunes >90% of branches immediately while keeping operand-1 transitions exact by pruning only prev < 1n rather than prev < target.

Using BigInt end-to-end prevents silent IEEE-754 overflow across 15-digit targets and cumulative sums, and parameterizing CalibrationOperator.tryInvert/explainPrune prepares Part 2 concatenation (||) with zero shared-module churn.

parts.title: Bridge Repair
parts.summary: Extend calibration equation repair by adding the decimal concatenation operator (||) alongside '+' and '*' under strict left-to-right evaluation, and return the sum of targets for all solvable equations.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn CONCAT_OPERATOR strategy plugging into 2024/day07/shared/ reverse-pruned DFS and BridgeRepairVisualizer with zero shared edits: computes exact BigInt base-10 scale (while scale <= right) and guards diff = remaining - right > 0n before testing diff % scale === 0n, solving 850 equations in 4.44 ms on the main thread; differentially verified against an independent forward string-concatenation DFS oracle across 260 seeded equations and power-of-10/suffix traps.
parts.complexity: O(M * 3^(k-1)) worst-case, ~O(M * k) typical time, O(k) space
learnings: Guarding diff = remaining - right <= 0n inside CONCAT_OPERATOR.tryInvert prevents the classic remaining === right false positive (0 || right), and while (scale <= right) handles every exact power of 10 in pure BigInt without string allocations.
Polymorphic CalibrationOperator + reusable BridgeRepairVisualizer delivered Part 2 in 73 lines of production domain code and a 7-line visualizer wrapper with zero edits to 2024/day07/shared/.

parts.title: Resonant Collinearity
parts.summary: On a 2D map of case-sensitive alphanumeric antennas, project the two exterior double-distance antinodes (2A - B and 2B - A) for every unordered same-frequency antenna pair and count unique in-bounds antinode locations.
parts.algorithmSummary: Frequency-grouped unordered pair projection into a flat Uint8Array(R * C) occupancy bitset parameterized by a polymorphic AntinodeProjectionRule (DOUBLE_DISTANCE_RULE) in 2024/day08/shared/ built on shared/core Grid2D (1.38 ms on 50x50 / 42 frequencies / 237 pairs), paired with a reusable ResonanceVisualizer in 2024/day08/shared/viz/ for zero-churn Part 2 harmonic reuse; differentially verified against both a global pair-hashset oracle and a cell-centric midpoint lookup oracle across 80 seeded grids.
parts.complexity: O(R * C + sum k_f^2) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Personal inputs deliberately include 16 matching uppercase/lowercase frequency pairs (e.g., 'a' vs 'A') and overlapping antinode-on-antenna hits, requiring case-sensitive frequency keys and separate occupancy tracking.
Parameterizing collectAntinodes, traceAntinodes, and ResonanceVisualizer by AntinodeProjectionRule prepares Part 2's full-line resonant harmonics with zero edits to 2024/day08/shared/.

parts.title: Resonant Collinearity
parts.summary: With resonant harmonics enabled, project every in-bounds grid lattice point collinear with at least two same-frequency antennas (including the antennas themselves whenever a frequency has two or more antennas) and count unique antinode positions.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn HARMONIC_LINE_RULE AntinodeProjectionRule plugging into 2024/day08/shared collectAntinodes, traceAntinodes, and ResonanceVisualizer with zero shared edits: reduces (dr, dc) by gcd(|dr|, |dc|) and steps forward and backward across the grid in O(R * C + sum(k_f^2) * max(R, C)) time (1.63 ms on 50x50 / 237 pairs); differentially verified against an independent cell-by-cell Euclidean cross-product collinearity oracle across both official examples and 60 seeded grids.
parts.complexity: O(R * C + sum(k_f^2) * max(R, C)) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Reducing (dr, dc) by gcd(|dr|, |dc|) guarantees exact Euclidean lattice collinearity even on non-coprime or axis-aligned pairs, while computing backward steps with 0 - sr avoids JavaScript -0 artifacts cleanly with zero extra branches.
Parameterizing AntinodeProjectionRule and ResonanceVisualizer in 2024/day08/shared/ delivered Part 2 in 100 lines of domain code and an 8-line visualizer wrapper with zero edits to shared/.

parts.title: Disk Fragmenter
parts.summary: Expand a dense alternating file/free-space digit disk map into block runs, compact files one block at a time from the rightmost file into the leftmost free space until no gaps remain between file blocks, and compute the exact filesystem checksum sum(position * fileId).
parts.algorithmSummary: Two-pointer extent-based compaction parameterized by CompactionStrategy in 2024/day09/shared/ using BigInt arithmetic-series range checksums and incremental deltaChecksum accounting in O(N) time (6.9 ms across 19,999 digits / ~95,000 blocks), paired with an encapsulated zero-copy DiskBlockReplay and dual-scale DiskStripSvg / DiskPlatterCanvas DiskCompactionVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 whole-file reuse; differentially verified against a flat block-by-block Int32Array swap oracle across 80 seeded random disk maps.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Operating directly on alternating file/gap extents with exact BigInt arithmetic-series checksums solves 95,000-block disk maps in 6.9 ms while keeping totalBlocks and initialChecksum dynamically derived from raw digits.

Separating CompactionStrategy, DiskBlockReplay, and the dual-scale DiskStripSvg / DiskPlatterCanvas visualizer in 2024/day09/shared/ prepares Part 2's whole-file compaction with zero shared-module churn.

parts.title: Disk Fragmenter
parts.summary: Compact the same alternating-digit disk map by moving whole files intact in strictly descending file-ID order (attempting each file at most once) into the leftmost contiguous free span strictly to the file's left that fits it, then compute the exact filesystem checksum.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn iterative Int32Array max-length segment tree (LeftmostSpanIndex.claimLeftmost) plugging into 2024/day09/shared CompactionStrategy, DiskBlockReplay, and DiskCompactionVisualizer with zero shared edits: coalesces adjacent initial free spans across zero-length files and performs O(log S) left-biased descents in O(N + F log S) time (9.33 ms on 19,999 digits / 10,000 files); differentially verified against both a coalesced linear-span oracle and a literal flat Int32Array block-array simulator across 100 zero-heavy PRNG disk maps.
parts.complexity: O(N + F log S) time, O(N) space
learnings: An iterative Int32Array max-length segment tree handles arbitrarily wide coalesced initial free spans (> 9 across zero-length files) natively in O(log S) per file with a narrow claimLeftmost(length, beforeStart) boundary that makes invalid index/over-consumption states impossible.

Because files move strictly left in descending ID order, vacated trailing extents can never sit left of any remaining unmoved file and never require re-insertion—verified end-to-end against a literal block-array simulator.

parts.title: Hoof It
parts.summary: On a 2D topographic elevation grid (0–9, with optional '.' barriers), score each height-0 trailhead by the number of distinct height-9 peaks reachable via strictly +1 orthogonal hiking trails, and return the sum of all trailhead scores.
parts.algorithmSummary: Generation-stamped height-ordered BFS (0 -> 9) using reusable encapsulated Int32Array buffers (queue capped at the exact Manhattan radius-9 lattice bound of 181 cells) parameterized by PeakContributionMetric (SCORE_METRIC) in 2024/day10/shared/ in O(V) time (4.41 ms on 57x57), paired with a HiDPI TopographicVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 rating reuse; differentially verified against an independent bottom-up 9 -> 0 BigInt bitset DP oracle (reusing shared/core bitCount) across all 5 official examples and 40 seeded random grids.
parts.complexity: O(V) time, O(V) space
learnings: A 9-step orthogonal hiking trail stays strictly inside Manhattan radius 9 (at most 181 cells) and FIFO order guarantees height-layered pops, so accumulating ways[nb] += ways[u] on revisit unifies Part 1 scores and Part 2 ratings in one O(V) kernel with zero shared edits.
Validating maxSteps via validateMaxSteps + sampleTraceIndices before short-circuiting empty trailhead lists catches invalid trace caps consistently even on zero-trailhead maps.

parts.title: Hoof It
parts.summary: Rate each height-0 trailhead on the topographic elevation grid by the total number of distinct strictly +1 orthogonal hiking trails from that trailhead to any height-9 peak, and return the sum of all trailhead ratings.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn RATING_METRIC strategy plugging into 2024/day10/shared generation-stamped height-ordered BFS and TopographicVisualizer (mode='rating') with zero shared edits in O(V) time (4.23 ms on 57x57): reuses exact per-cell path multiplicity accumulation (ways[nb] += ways[u], bounded by 4 * 3^8 = 26,244 << 2^31) and renders numeric peak path-count badges; differentially verified against both a global bottom-up 9 -> 0 elevation DP oracle up to 57x57 and an explicit unmemoized 10-cell path-enumeration DFS oracle.
parts.complexity: O(V) time, O(V) space
learnings: Because every reachable cell at elevation h >= 1 has out-degree <= 3 to elevation h + 1, any single trailhead's rating is strictly <= 4 * 3^8 = 26,244—making Int32Array path accumulation provably overflow-free.

Parameterizing PeakContributionMetric and TopographicVisualizer(mode='rating') in 2024/day10/shared/ delivered Part 2 in 43 lines of production domain code and a 16-line visualizer wrapper with zero shared-module edits.

parts.title: Plutonian Pebbles
parts.summary: Evolve a line of integer-engraved stones through 25 simultaneous blinks—mapping 0 to 1, splitting even-digit numbers into two half-length stones with leading zeros stripped, and multiplying all other stones by 2024—and return the total stone count.
parts.algorithmSummary: Order-independent frequency-histogram DP in exact BigInt (Map<bigint, bigint> with per-run memoized blinkStone) parameterized by blinkCount via createPlutonianPebblesSolver(25) in 2024/day11/shared/ in O(B * D) time (1.93 ms across 25 blinks), paired with a dual-curve log10 GrowthChartSvg (reusing shared/core bigintLog2) and PebbleEvolutionVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 (75-blink) reuse; differentially verified against both a literal ordered-array oracle (blinks 0..12) and a top-down memoized recursive DP oracle (up to 75 blinks) plus superposition invariance.
parts.complexity: O(B * D) time, O(D) space
learnings: Collapsing stones into a Map<bigint, bigint> frequency histogram turns exponential stone counts into O(B * D) exact BigInt updates while keeping DEFAULT_MAX_TRACE_STEPS = 80 large enough to capture every single blink of both Part 1 (25) and Part 2 (75).

Avoiding Math.log10 on BigInt values in blinkStone and computing visualizer rule percentages via Number((part * 1000n) / total) / 10 keeps both domain transitions and UI bars exact across arbitrary BigInt magnitudes.

parts.title: Plutonian Pebbles
parts.summary: Evolve the same line of integer-engraved stones through 75 simultaneous blinks and return the exact total stone count.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn PART2_BLINKS = 75 specialization reusing 2024/day11/shared frequency-histogram DP and PebbleEvolutionVisualizer with zero shared edits (33.69 ms in exact BigInt across 75 blinks / ~3,800 distinct attractor values, tracing all 76 blinks 1:1 under DEFAULT_MAX_TRACE_STEPS = 80); differentially verified against both a pure-arithmetic top-down memoized recursive DP oracle (using / and % digit splitting) and a Chapman-Kolmogorov semigroup split (37 + 38 = 75) oracle.
parts.complexity: O(B * D) time, O(D) space
learnings: Even though total stones explode past 2.48e14 at 75 blinks, repeated even-digit splitting collapses distinct values into a ~3,800-label attractor, solving Part 2 in 33.69 ms in exact BigInt with 7 lines of production domain code and zero edits to 2024/day11/shared/.
Cross-checking against both pure-arithmetic top-down memoized DP and a 37+38 Chapman-Kolmogorov semigroup split independently validates both intermediate histograms and digit-splitting transitions.

parts.title: Garden Groups
parts.summary: Partition a 2D uppercase garden plot grid into 4-connected same-plant regions, compute each region's fencing price as area * perimeter, and return the total fencing cost across all regions.
parts.algorithmSummary: Single-pass flat Int32Array BFS region flood-fill parameterized by a polymorphic RegionFenceMetric (PERIMETER_METRIC) in 2024/day12/shared/ in O(R * C) time (12.58 ms on 140x140): stores region labels and cells in immutable GardenRegions and pairs with a HiDPI GardenCanvas and GardenGroupsVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 (bulk-discount sides) reuse; differentially verified against an independent shared/core DisjointSet connected-component oracle across all official examples, nested enclaves, and 50 seeded random grids.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Factoring RegionFenceMetric (evaluating a single connected region against the immutable GardenMap) into 2024/day12/shared/ prepares Part 2's straight-side/corner bulk discount with zero edits to shared/ or part1/.

Cross-checking flat Int32Array BFS flood-fill against shared/core DisjointSet connected components independently verifies nested holes, diagonal touchings of identical plant types, and single-plot islands.

parts.title: Garden Groups
parts.summary: Under the bulk discount, compute each 4-connected garden region's fencing price as area * sides (where each continuous straight fence segment counts as one side, with kissing diagonal corners staying separate) and return the total cost.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn 4-quadrant convex/concave corner-counting SIDES_METRIC plugging into 2024/day12/shared RegionPartition and GardenGroupsVisualizer with zero shared edits in O(R * C) time (14.12 ms on 140x140): queries partition.sameRegion(regionId, r, c) across all 4 diagonal quadrants so outer, interior-hole, and Möbius kissing-diagonal corners are counted exactly without segment materialization; differentially verified against an independent DisjointSet + directed outward-normal fence-edge run-merging oracle across all 5 official examples, pinch diagonals, nested enclaves, and 50 seeded random grids.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Counting convex (!sameV && !sameH) and concave (sameV && sameH && !sameDiag) corners via partition.sameRegion(region.id, ...) handles kissing-diagonal/Möbius pinches and nested holes automatically in O(1) auxiliary space with zero edits to 2024/day12/shared/.
Cross-checking corner counting against a directed outward-normal (N/S/E/W) fence-edge run-merging oracle independently confirms that opposite-facing edges at pinch vertices never merge.

parts.title: Claw Contraption
parts.summary: For each two-button claw machine (Button A costs 3 tokens, Button B costs 1 token, max 100 presses per button), compute the minimum tokens required to align the claw exactly with each winnable prize and return the total token spend.
parts.algorithmSummary: Exact BigInt Cramer's rule with complete collinear 1D extended-GCD + shared/core ceilDiv/floorDiv interval minimization parameterized by ClawConfig(prizeOffset=0n, maxPresses=100n) in 2024/day13/shared/ in O(M) non-singular time (1.10 ms across 320 machines), paired with a BigInt-safe ray-projection ClawVectorDiagram and ClawContraptionVisualizer for zero-churn Part 2 (10^13 offset, unbounded presses) reuse; differentially verified against an independent brute-force (A, B) in [0..100]^2 minimizer oracle across official examples, curated collinear/tie/cap boundaries, and 150 seeded random machines.
parts.complexity: O(M) non-singular, O(M log max(ax, bx)) worst-case time, O(M) space
learnings: Solving 2x2 claw systems via exact BigInt Cramer's rule and falling back to 1D extended-GCD interval minimization with cost slope (3 * aStep - bStep) when det === 0n makes the shared solver both mathematically complete and overflow-free for Part 2's 10^13 offset.
Projecting unwinnable button rays onto the bounding box via BigInt cross-multiplication before normalizing prevents ray underflow to (0, 0) when Part 2 prizes jump to 10^13 scale.

parts.title: Claw Contraption
parts.summary: Shift every claw machine prize coordinate upward by 10,000,000,000,000 on both axes with no upper press limit and compute the exact minimum total tokens needed to win all winnable prizes.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn PART2_CONFIG = new ClawConfig(10_000_000_000_000n, null) specialization reusing 2024/day13/shared exact BigInt Cramer's rule, collinear extended-GCD minimization, and BigInt-safe ClawContraptionVisualizer with zero shared edits (0.90 ms across 320 machines, totaling 92.87 trillion tokens in exact BigInt); differentially verified against an independent shared/core Rational 2x2 Gauss-Jordan elimination and modular-inverse collinear oracle across official examples (875318608908n), curated 10^13 edge cases, and 150 seeded random machines.
parts.complexity: O(M) non-singular, O(M log max(ax, bx)) worst-case time, O(M) space
learnings: Parameterizing ClawConfig(prizeOffset, maxPresses) and using exact BigInt arithmetic in 2024/day13/shared/ reduced Part 2 (10^13 offset, unbounded presses) to 10 lines of domain code and a 14-line visualizer wrapper running in 0.90 ms with zero edits to shared/.

Cross-checking BigInt Cramer + extended-GCD against shared/core Rational 2x2 Gauss-Jordan elimination and modular-inverse collinear minimization independently validates 10^15-scale cross products and arbitrary determinant signs.

parts.title: Restroom Redoubt
parts.summary: Simulate robots with constant velocities wrapping around a 101x103 toroidal room for 100 seconds, count robots strictly inside each of the four quadrants (excluding centerlines), and multiply the four counts to compute the safety factor.
parts.algorithmSummary: Overflow-safe O(N) closed-form modular teleportation using shared/core euclideanMod(euclideanMod(pos, size) + euclideanMod(vel, size) * (seconds % size), size) in 2024/day14/shared/ (0.84 ms across 500 robots): encapsulates a private Uint32Array occupancy buffer inside immutable RedoubtSnapshot with dynamic getters (quadrants, safetyFactor, uniqueCells, adjacentPairs) and pairs with a HiDPI Canvas 2D RedoubtCanvas for zero-churn Part 2 Christmas-tree clustering reuse; differentially verified against an independent tick-by-tick t = 1..T simulator across the 11x7 example (12), single-robot trajectories, multi-period wraps, crosshair exclusions, stacked cells, and 60 seeded random swarms.
parts.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Pre-reducing seconds % size before multiplying by euclideanMod(vel, size) prevents safe-integer overflow at arbitrarily large horizons while computing exact wrapped positions in O(1) per robot.

Exposing fillOccupancy, countAdjacentOccupied, RedoubtSnapshot (zero stored derived state), and RedoubtCanvas in 2024/day14/shared/ prepares Part 2's Christmas-tree clustering search with zero shared-module churn.

parts.title: Restroom Redoubt
parts.summary: Find the earliest second at which the wrapping robots on the 101x103 toroidal grid align into the hidden Christmas tree picture.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn 2-pass Uint32Array generation-stamped orthogonal adjacency peak scan across the full lcm(W, H) torus period reusing 2024/day14/shared TorusSpace, Robot, RedoubtSnapshot, and RedoubtCanvas with zero shared edits (54.78 ms across 10,403 frames / 500 robots, detecting an 11.5x adjacency spike of 532 pairs vs 46.4 baseline mean at the exact framed tree): uses Pass-1 unique-cell stamping plus Pass-2 non-wrapping right/down neighbor counting for exact order-independent parity with countAdjacentOccupied and pairs with a max-pooled AdjacencySparkline SVG and Jump-to-Peak playback; differentially verified against both exact per-frame countAdjacentOccupied parity and an independent BigInt minimum-variance + Extended-Euclidean CRT oracle on the 15x13 synthetic tree (42) and a seeded 500-robot 101x103 swarm.
parts.complexity: O(N * lcm(W, H)) time, O(W * H + N) space
learnings: Separating each frame into Pass 1 (generation-stamped unique cell collection + robot stepping) and Pass 2 (counting non-wrapping right/down pairs across unique occupied cells) eliminates grid zeroing while guaranteeing exact order-independent parity with countAdjacentOccupied.

Cross-checking full-period adjacency peak detection against an independent BigInt minimum-variance + CRT oracle and visually inspecting the rendered frame confirms the framed Christmas tree with zero guesswork.

parts.title: Warehouse Woes
parts.summary: Simulate a robot executing directional moves inside a walled warehouse pushing contiguous lines of 1x1 boxes ('O') whenever an open floor tile lies behind them, and return the sum of all box GPS coordinates (100 * row + col).
parts.algorithmSummary: Flat Uint8Array ray-scan with O(1) endpoint-swap push (PART1_PUSH_RULE) behind a polymorphic WarehouseRule strategy in 2024/day15/shared/ in O(M * L) time (4.79 ms across 50x50 grid / 20,000 moves): encapsulates terrain and robot coordinates inside WarehouseState/immutable WarehouseSnapshot (never freezing TypedArrays, deriving gpsSum over both 'O' and '[' dynamically) and pairs with a HiDPI WarehouseCanvas/WarehouseVisualizer (already supporting linked wide '[]' crates) for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against an independent string[][] tail-to-head shift oracle across all 15 steps of the small example (2028), the large example final board (10092), and 50 seeded random warehouses.
parts.complexity: O(M * L) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Returning immutable WarehouseSnapshot copies from runWarehouseSimulation and WarehouseFrame keeps Uint8Array mutation strictly encapsulated inside WarehouseState while deriving gpsSum and boxCount dynamically with zero stored derived state.
Supporting both 'O' and paired '[]' tiles in WarehouseState.fromRows, gpsSum, and WarehouseCanvas prepares Part 2's doubled warehouse and branching vertical box pushes with zero shared-module churn.

parts.title: Warehouse Woes
parts.summary: Double the warehouse map horizontally ('#' -> '##', 'O' -> '[]', '.' -> '..', '@' -> '@.'), simulate the robot pushing linked 2-wide crates horizontally in rows and vertically across branching/converging DAGs (aborting atomically if any pushed crate hits a wall), and return the sum of all crate GPS coordinates (100 * row + leftCol).
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn PART2_PUSH_RULE plugging into 2024/day15/shared WarehouseState, createWarehouseSolver, and WarehouseVisualizer with zero shared edits in O(M * K_avg) time (6.02 ms across 50x100 widened grid / 20,000 moves): runs 1D ray-shift on horizontal pushes and iterative Set-deduplicated BFS closure with 2-pass clear-then-write updates on vertical DAG pushes so diamond merges shift once and blocked branches abort with zero partial mutation; differentially verified against an independent memoized recursive canPush + copy-on-write string[][] oracle across all 11 steps of the small example (618), the large example final board (9021), diamond/asymmetric partial blocks, and 50 seeded random warehouses.
parts.complexity: O(M * K_avg) time, O(R * C) space
learnings: Iterative BFS closure with Set<number> deduplication and 2-pass clear-then-write prevents double-shifting in diamond box merges and guarantees atomic zero-mutation rollbacks on asymmetric partial blocks.
Because 2024/day15/shared already supported linked '['/']' tiles in WarehouseState, gpsSum, and WarehouseCanvas, Part 2 required zero edits to shared/ and zero imports from part1/.

parts.title: Reindeer Maze
parts.summary: Find the minimum score to guide a reindeer starting at S facing East to reach E in a walled maze, where stepping forward costs 1 point and rotating 90 degrees clockwise or counterclockwise in place costs 1,000 points.
parts.algorithmSummary: Flat typed-array binary-heap Dijkstra (StateMinHeap over Float64Array distances indexed by (cell << 2) | dir) + implicit tight-edge backward BFS in 2024/day16/shared/ in O(W * H * log(W * H)) time (7.74 ms on 141x141): early-stops only once popped cost > bestScore so all optimal multi-heading E arrivals are finalized, extracts the exact optimalTileMask via O(V_opt) backward tight-edge BFS and a zero-dead-branch canonical shortest path, and exposes a polymorphic MazeObjective + HiDPI ReindeerMazeCanvas (with showAllOptimalTiles toggle) for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against an independent forward + explicit reverse-graph FIFO SPFA oracle across official Examples 1 (7036 / 45 tiles) & 2 (11048 / 64 tiles), multi-heading ties, unreachable/walled-off starts, and 40 seeded random mazes.
parts.complexity: O(W * H * log(W * H)) time, O(W * H) space
learnings: Stopping forward Dijkstra at popped cost > bestScore (rather than on the first E pop) guarantees every state on every optimal path is settled, letting an allocation-free O(V_opt) tight-edge backward BFS compute Part 2's exact optimalTileMask with zero edits to 2024/day16/shared/.

Because per-cell minCellDist(S) can be 0 when S is walled off, normalizing the canvas distance gradient with branch-free Math.max(1, maxCellMinDist) prevents division-by-zero without introducing an unreachable V8 coverage branch.

parts.title: Reindeer Maze
parts.summary: Count every distinct maze tile (including S and E) that lies on at least one minimum-score path from (S, East) to E.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn part2Objective specialization reusing 2024/day16/shared forward Dijkstra (stopping at popped cost > bestScore), implicit tight-edge backward BFS (MazeAnalysis.optimalTileCount), and ReindeerMazeVisualizer with showAllOptimalTiles={true} with zero shared edits (8.16 ms on 141x141): seeds all tied optimal (E, dir) states and walks incoming tight transitions (dist[prev] + w === dist[cur]) to populate the deduplicated optimal tile mask rendered in amber; differentially verified against both an independent Bidirectional Dijkstra oracle (distStart[(c<<2)|d] + distEnd[(c<<2)|d] === bestScore across official Examples 1 (45) & 2 (64), ties, and 30 seeded random mazes) and an Exhaustive State-Visited DFS oracle on tie-heavy <= 7x7 mazes.
parts.complexity: O(W * H * log(W * H)) time, O(W * H) space
learnings: Pre-computing the O(V_opt) tight-edge backward BFS optimalMask and showAllOptimalTiles canvas layer inside 2024/day16/shared/ reduced Part 2 to an 11-line MazeObjective and 15-line visualizer wrapper with zero shared edits.

Bidirectional Dijkstra differential verification must check distStart[(c<<2)|d] + distEnd[(c<<2)|d] === bestScore per identical directed state (c, d) rather than taking separate per-cell minimums across headings.

parts.title: Chronospatial Computer
parts.summary: Simulate a 3-bit virtual machine with three arbitrary-precision registers (A, B, C) and 8 opcodes (adv, bxl, bst, jnz, bxc, out, bdv, cdv) over a program tape of 3-bit integers and return the comma-joined output stream.
parts.algorithmSummary: Table-driven arbitrary-precision BigInt 3-bit VM (OPCODE_TABLE + COMBO_RESOLVERS) in 2024/day17/shared/ in O(T * W) time (0.39 ms on personal input): enforces non-negative BigInt registers ready for Part 2's ~48-bit quine A, handles odd-IP jnz jumps and dynamic runtime combo-7 validation (keeping literal/ignored 7 in bxl/jnz/bxc valid), uses shift-safe divPow2 without huge 2^k allocations, exposes 2-pass bounded-memory traceProgram and interactive ChronospatialDebugger (with decimal/octal/binary RegisterPanel, DisassemblyTape, and Part 2 targetOutput/extraPanel hooks) for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against an independent textbook switch-based BigInt VM oracle across all 5 short official examples, main example (4,6,3,5,6,3,5,2,1,0), 64-bit registers, odd-IP jumps, and 100 seeded synthetic programs.
parts.complexity: O(T * W) time, O(P + K) space
learnings: Using non-negative BigInt registers and shift-safe divPow2 (returning 0n when shift >= bitLength) prevents 32-bit JS bitwise truncation and prepares Part 2's ~48-bit quine search with zero shared-module edits.

Validating reserved combo operand 7 dynamically inside resolveCombo (rather than at parse time) preserves valid literal/ignored 7 instructions (bxl 7, jnz 7, bxc 7) while placing disassembleProgram in opcodes.ts keeps the internal DAG strictly acyclic.

parts.title: Chronospatial Computer
parts.summary: Find the lowest positive initial Register A value that causes the 3-bit Chronospatial VM program to emit an exact copy of its own instructions (a self-reproducing quine).
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn backward 3-bit octal DFS + live BigInt VM suffix verification reusing 2024/day17/shared ChronospatialProgram, runProgram, traceProgram, and ChronospatialDebugger (with targetOutput match highlighting and a QuineOctalPanel reconstruction table) with zero shared edits (2.75 ms on 16-token 48-bit personal quine): searches pos = N - 1 down to 0 trying ascending octal digits (skipping leading 0 when prefix === 0n) so the first leaf reached is guaranteed globally minimal across both adv-before-out and adv-after-out loop layouts; differentially verified against both a brute-force minimality proof on 0,3,5,4,3,0 (117440) and an independent non-recursive backward-octal-BFS all-quines oracle across official and multi-branching 16-token synthetic programs.
parts.complexity: O(V * N * L) time (V ~ 50-500 visited octal nodes), O(N) stack space
learnings: Backward 3-bit octal DFS with startDigit = (prefix === 0n ? 1 : 0) enumerates exact N-octal-digit positive integers in strictly ascending order, working uniformly whether adv 3 runs before or after out with zero hardcoded algebra.

Deriving QuineReconstructionStep.candidate and QuineSearchResult.registerA via getters eliminates stored derived state while reusing ChronospatialDebugger's targetOutput and extraPanel hooks delivered Part 2 with zero edits to 2024/day17/shared/.

parts.title: RAM Run
parts.summary: Simulate the first 1,024 falling byte coordinates corrupting cells on a 71x71 memory grid and find the minimum number of orthogonal steps from (0, 0) to (70, 70).
parts.algorithmSummary: Immutable MemorySpace recording each cell's earliest fall index in a flat Int32Array + flat Int32Array 4-neighbor BFS in 2024/day18/shared/ (3.48 ms on 71x71 / 1024 bytes): stores firstFallIndex once so both Part 1 shortest-path BFS and Part 2 reverse-time DisjointSet percolation reuse the same model with zero shared edits, paired with HiDPI RamRunCanvas (already supporting crimson blockingByte highlight for Part 2) and dual-config manifest (7x7/12 example vs 71x71/1024 personal); differentially verified against an independent Set<string> BFS oracle across 60 seeded grids and a reverse-time DisjointSet percolation oracle.
parts.complexity: O(W * H + B) time, O(W * H) space
learnings: Recording each grid cell's earliest fall index in a flat Int32Array (NEVER_CORRUPTED = Int32 max) turns time-sliced queries into O(1) comparisons and makes Part 2 reverse-time DSU percolation zero-churn.

Handling 7x7 / 12 vs 71x71 / 1024 configuration via createRamRunPart1Solver keeps domain logic pure while allowing the CLI to default to 71x71 / 1024 and the UI manifest to recognize the official example.

parts.title: RAM Run
parts.summary: Find the first falling byte coordinate in the full corruption stream whose landing permanently severs all orthogonal paths from (0, 0) to (70, 70).
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reverse-time DisjointSet percolation reusing 2024/day18/shared MemorySpace, findShortestPath, createStaticSnapshot, RamRunCanvas, and shared/core DisjointSet with zero shared edits (3.53 ms on 71x71 / 3,450 bytes): activates all never-corrupted cells first, then unwinds k from B down until (0, 0) and (S - 1, S - 1) are both open and connected (activating cell idx only when firstFall[idx] === k so duplicate coordinates cannot prematurely reopen blocked cells); differentially verified against both a binary-search BFS oracle (80 seeded grids including duplicates, 1x1, and endpoint hits) and a linear forward BFS oracle (25 small grids).
parts.complexity: O(S^2 + B * alpha(S^2)) time, O(S^2) space
learnings: Reverse-time DisjointSet percolation checking firstFall[idx] === k and open[0] === 1 && open[goalIdx] === 1 handles duplicate byte coordinates, direct endpoint hits, and 1x1 grids cleanly in a single O(S^2 + B * alpha(S^2)) pass.
Omitting a redundant k > 0 loop guard when termination at k = 0 is mathematically guaranteed preserves 100% V8 branch coverage without artificial dead-code branches.

parts.title: Linen Layout
parts.summary: Given an unlimited supply of available 5-color towel stripe patterns and a list of desired towel designs, count how many designs can be assembled by concatenating available patterns.
parts.algorithmSummary: Preallocated flat 5-way Int32Array PatternTrie + unbounded exact BigInt bottom-up DP in 2024/day19/shared/ (7.07 ms across 447 patterns and 400 designs): encodes {w,u,b,r,g} as 0..4 for zero-allocation Trie transitions, computes exact prefixWays: bigint[] and canonical witnessDecomposition in a single O(L * M) pass per design (exposing countTotalArrangements and LinenVisualizer mode='possible' | 'arrangements' with bigintLog2-scaled SVG prefix bars for zero-churn Part 2 reuse); differentially verified against an independent recursive memoized startsWith DP oracle (30 seeded sets), exhaustive short-string partition enumeration, > 2^64 BigInt overflow stress, and dead-end backtracking traps.
parts.complexity: O(sum(|p|) + D * L * M) time, O(5 * N_trie + L) space
learnings: Preallocating a flat 5-way Int32Array Trie to 1 + sum(|p|) eliminates dynamic resize branches and substring allocations while unbounded bigint[] DP prevents overflow even past BigInt64Array max (2^63 - 1).
Looping i from prefixWays.length - 1 down to i > 0 in furthestReachable avoids an unreachable loop-exit branch under V8 coverage since prefixWays[0] === 1n is always guaranteed.

parts.title: Linen Layout
parts.summary: Sum the exact number of distinct ordered ways each desired towel design can be assembled from available patterns across all 400 designs.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn exact BigInt arrangement counter reusing 2024/day19/shared PatternTrie, unbounded bigint[] countTotalArrangements, buildLinenTrace, and LinenVisualizer (mode='arrangements') with zero shared edits (6.74 ms across 447 patterns and 400 designs, total ~7.33 x 10^14); differentially verified against both an independent recursive memoized startsWith BigInt oracle (official example 16n + 20 seeded random multi-design layouts) and an exhaustive small-design backtracking partition counter, plus > (1n << 63n) - 1n odd-low-bit precision, duplicate design summing, and duplicate pattern deduplication tests.
parts.complexity: O(sum(|p|) + D * L * M) time, O(5 * N_trie + L) space
learnings: Passing parseLinenLayout, solvePart2, and buildLinenTrace directly into Object.freeze({...}) keeps Part 2's domain solver at 19 lines with zero wrapper branches and zero edits to 2024/day19/shared/.
Testing an odd BigInt sum strictly above (1n << 63n) - 1n proves exactness beyond both IEEE-754 safe integers and signed 64-bit BigInt64Array limits.

parts.title: Race Condition
parts.summary: Find every single-use collision-disabled cheat lasting up to 2 picoseconds on a 141x141 racetrack that saves at least 100 picoseconds compared to the shortest uncheated S-to-E path.
parts.algorithmSummary: Dual flat-Int32Array BFS (distFromStart & distFromEnd) + row/col-clamped Manhattan diamond scanner in 2024/day20/shared/ (6.80 ms on 141x141): works on both unique-path AoC grids and general branching/looping tracks, breaks early via monotonic BFS distance (distU <= baseline - minSaving - 2) with zero dead V8 branches, records 1 canonical witness per saving bucket in O(baseline) TypedArrays, and ships PART2_DEFAULT_CONFIG (K=20, minSaving=100) + HiDPI RacetrackCanvas (with translucent Manhattan radius halo) + SavingHistogram for zero-churn Part 2 reuse; differentially verified against both an O(T^2) all-pairs Manhattan oracle and a per-cheat full-BFS oracle across official examples (44 P1, 285 P2), branching/pocket tracks, and 20 seeded mazes for K in {2, 4, 10, 20}.
parts.complexity: O(W * H + T * K^2) time, O(W * H) space
learnings: Using distFromStart[reachable[i]] <= maxStartDist as the loop condition in analyzeCheats eliminates an unreachable loop-exit branch under V8 coverage because E is guaranteed in reachable at distance baseline > maxStartDist.
Adding a borderless track grid to bfs.test.ts exercises all four out-of-bounds BFS neighbor guards that walled AoC grids never hit.
